newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rail intermodal freight up from year ago--AAR.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rail intermodal freight up from year ago--AAR.

text.p: U.S. rail intermodal freight rose in the week ended May 31 from the same year-earlier week, the Association of American Railroads said on Thursday.
AAR said intermodal freight, which does not include carloads, increased 8.1 percent to 150,496 trailers and containers in the week, compared with 139,170 in the year-earlier week.
AAR attributed the surge to the increasing strength of foreign economies, decreasing motor carriers capacity and an increase in intermodal usage by motor carriers.

It said total carloads were 327,530 in the week, up 1.4 percent from 323,096 in the year-ago week, while ton-miles rose 1.7 percent to 24.6 billion, from 24.2 billion a year ago. A ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, is one ton of freight hauled one mile.
Loadings of grain were up 7.9 percent to 19,394 from 17,970 loadings a year ago, while coal carloads fell 4.6 percent to 122,539 from 128,465 carloads.

The motor vehicles and equipment sector saw a sharp increase in carloads in the latest week, up 14 percent to 18,710 carloads, from 16,412 carloads the same week a year ago. Farm products also increased, rising 7.4 percent to 1,599 carloads from 1,489 a year ago, AAR said.

In the first 22 weeks of 1997, AAR said carloads increased 1.8 percent to 7.45 million from 7.32 million in the same 1996 period. Trailers and containers rose 6.6 percent to 3.54 million from 3.33 million, while ton-miles increased 2.3 percent in the period to 582.1 billion, from 568.9 billion.

For the first 22 weeks of 1997, AAR reported that the two Canadian-based railroads had 1.16 million carloads, up 1.2 percent from the year-ago period, and 532,632 trailers and containers, up 10.8 percent from last year, AAR said.

Combined total volume in the United States and Canada for the first 22 weeks was 8.61 million carloads, up 1.7 percent from the same 1996 period, while intermodal traffic totaled 4.08 million trailers and containers, up 7.1 percent from last year, AAR said.
